title: Gonux
summary: Gonux is a Southold placename for a point on Great Hog Neck, also called Peconic Park. the point was named for Moses Gonack, who drowned nearby and was buried there.
address_label: Great Hog Neck / Peconic Park, Town of Southold, NY
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Gonux and Gonack. The name is connected with Algonquian words describing height or length, including meanings such as long, tall, or high, and compared with words for a tall person.

Why Place Names Matter

“Systematic analysis of place names highlights both presence and displacements of cultural memory and offers potential for an additional rich layer of interpretation in landscape characterisation.”

— Meryem Atik and Simon Swaffield, Place Names and Landscape Character: a Case Study (2017), Abstract
land_loss_content: Gonux preserves a personal name, a death record, and a remembered burial point in the Southold landscape. Native lives and local memory can remain attached to small coastal points even when the physical marker is no longer visible.
whereintheworld_content: The map placement uses the Great Hog Neck / Peconic Park area as a public reference, not an exact burial or grave-marker coordinate.
